chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Bakr, from Hafs, from Umar ibn Salim, and Muhammad ibn Ziyad ibn Isa, from Harun ibn Harizah, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Count Sha'ban as twenty-nine days; if it is cloudy, then become a fasting person in the morning; and if it is clear, and you look closely and see nothing (the moon), then become a non-fasting person in the morning.'

key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: The eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, preceding Ramadan.
key_terms.صَائِماً: Fasting, indicating the commencement of the Ramadan fast.
key_terms.مُتَغَيِّمَةً: Cloudy or overcast, obscuring the view of the moon.
key_terms.مُصْحِيَةً: Clear or bright, allowing for clear visibility.
key_terms.مُفْطِراً: Not fasting, indicating the continuation of the current month (Sha'ban) for one more day.

ai.seo_question: How to determine the start of Ramadan when the moon is not visible due to weather conditions?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a nuanced legal principle for determining the start of Ramadan by distinguishing between obscured visibility and clear skies without sighting. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential preference for 'Istikmal' (completing thirty days) when uncertainty persists, ensuring the fast is not prematurely entered. It highlights the practical application of lunar observation within the Ahl al-Bayt's methodology, balancing astronomical clarity with religious caution.
